sections.label: Bill enhances NParks marine park protection
sections.summary: The Bill enhances NParks' ability to protect the Sisters' Islands Marine Park.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: First, the Bill enhances NParks' ability to protect the Sisters' Islands Marine Park, or SIMP.

sections.label: Marine park definition in Parks and Trees Act
sections.summary: Adding a marine park definition and public park type makes the Parks and Trees Act apply to the designated foreshore and marine areas.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: By adding a definition of "marine park" in clause 2(a) and adding it as a type of public park in clause 2(c), we make it clear that the protection of the Parks and Trees Act applies to the designated foreshore as well as marine areas in the Sisters' Islands Marine Park.

sections.label: Offence for abandoning aquatic pets
sections.summary: Clause 5 makes it an offence to release or abandon animals into watercourses outside nature reserves that flow into the reserves.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: However, the law currently does not cover cases where unwanted aquatic pets like exotic fish and terrapins are abandoned in streams or drains that lead into the reserves.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: So, clause 5 now makes it an offence for any person to release or abandon animals into watercourses outside of our nature reserves, if the person knows or ought to know that these watercourses flow into the reserves.

sections.label: NParks can order greenery reinstatement
sections.summary: Clause 10 allows NParks to order those responsible to also reinstate the greenery.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Clause 10 now allows NParks to order those responsible to also reinstate the greenery.

sections.label: Planting dimensions moved to subsidiary legislation
sections.summary: It transfers prescription of planting area dimensions to subsidiary legislation and lets the Commissioner modify or waive them.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Sometimes, this hinders the adoption of innovative greenery proposals like vertical planting.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: It transfers the prescription of dimensions of planting areas from the Parks and Trees Act to subsidiary legislation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: It also allows the Commissioner to modify or waive these dimensions where necessary or appropriate.

sections.label: Landscape Productivity Grant launched in 2013
sections.summary: In 2013, NParks launched the Landscape Productivity Grant to help companies mechanise.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: In 2013, NParks launched the Landscape Productivity Grant to help companies mechanise.

sections.label: NParks managing nursery State land
sections.summary: The clause empowers NParks to manage State land for nurseries, tendered in phases from mid-2018 for nurseries affected by redevelopment.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: In particular, the clause empowers NParks to manage and optimise State land safeguarded for nurseries.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: This land will be tendered out in phases from mid-2018 to provide options for nurseries affected by redevelopment plans.

sections.label: Question on neighbours' options
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Minister can advise what neighbours can do in such cases.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister advise, in such cases, what can the neighbours do?

sections.label: Tree trimming law and NParks
sections.summary: The Government is amending the law to let NParks direct owners to trim dangerous trees, and asks about the danger definition and cutting disputed trees.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This has made the residents feel rather helpless.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Now, the Government is amending the law to allow NParks to direct property owners to trim trees that could pose a danger to others.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This would give the residents peace of mind.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: However, I would like to ask the Minister: what is the definition of "posing a danger to others"?

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As for the trees that cause dispute, can NParks have the trees cut down?

sections.label: Survey discovered new species
sections.summary: In five years the Survey discovered possibly 100 new species, a major accomplishment and contribution to the global commons.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In the five years, the Survey has discovered possibly 100 new species, which is, in itself, a major accomplishment and contribution to the global commons.

sections.label: Restrictions under Act sections
sections.summary: Sections 8 and 9 restrict collecting, capturing and displacing plants and animals and disturbing land, amid more visitors to marine biodiversity.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Under sections 8 and 9 of the Act, persons are restricted from collecting, capturing and displacing any plants and animals; from disturbing the land This is more urgent, given that intertidal guided walks are being conducted and the diving trail and other planned trails will bring more visitors to experience the marine biodiversity up close.

sections.label: Scale of marine park protection
sections.summary: The marine park covers 40 hectares around Sisters' Island and reefs off western Pulau Tekukor and St John's Island.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: My second disappointment is with the scale of the protection.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The marine park covers 40 hectares around Sisters' Island and the reefs off the western coasts of Pulau Tekukor and St John's Island.

sections.label: Marine park split into three parts
sections.summary: The marine park is split into three parts off Sisters' Islands, St John's and Pulau Tekukor, and a 2024 collision nearby raised oil spill fears.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The marine park, as it is designated now, is not a contiguous zone of protection, but split into three parts off Sisters' Islands, St John's and Pulau Tekukor.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Just last year, in August, a collision between a Very Large Crude Carrier and a container ship close to the Sisters' Island brought on fears of an oil spill that would have been disastrous for the marine park.

sections.label: Clause 4 designates park managers
sections.summary: Clause 4 inserts a new section 6A letting the Minister designate any entity to manage a public park.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Clause 4 of the Bill inserts a new section 6A to allow the Minister to designate any entity to manage a public park.

sections.label: Marine park management may be reassigned
sections.summary: Because the marine park is a public park, its management could be assigned to an entity other than NParks.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: With respect to the marine park being defined as a public park, rather than a national park or natural reserve, this new section means that the management of the marine park could be assigned to another entity other than NParks.

sections.label: Other areas and threatening trees
sections.summary: It asks whether other areas besides Sisters' Islands are considered, and notes NParks can act on trees posing immediate threat.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: With the definition of marine park given in section 2, Part 3, are there other parks or areas that are under consideration, besides the Sister's Islands and its vicinity, which have been stipulated in the Bill, and how actively are we working with other expert groups to see if there are other suggested areas that can be incorporated into this?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Thirdly, for trees found in any premises and are deemed to pose an immediate threat to life and property, it is known that NParks can intervene and take necessary action.

sections.label: Roadside tree pruning intervals
sections.summary: It asks whether there are regular timelines for pruning roadside trees in residential areas, noting work seems done only when activated.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Fourthly, for trees found on our roadside within residential areas and estates, can I check if there are regular timelines or intervals for pruning and trimming?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: From the numerous observations I have made, it seems to be carried out only when we activate NParks or the relevant agencies or in situations when the trees are overgrown, are encasing street lamps, or are attracting numerous birds.

sections.label: Parks and Trees Amendment Bill aims
sections.summary: The Bill updates the Parks and Trees Act to expand NParks powers, raise penalties and extend protections to marine parks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Parks and Trees (Amendment) Bill seeks to update the Parks and Trees Act to expand the powers of NParks to appoint park rangers, to increase penalties for nature-related offences and to extend certain protections to marine parks, among other things.

sections.label: Tree removal last resort
sections.summary: The reply stated that tree removal is a last resort.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The reply was that tree removal is a last resort.

sections.label: Consultation on tree replanting
sections.summary: NParks and HDB could consult residents where many trees are removed and replanted or new trees planted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Where a significant number of trees are to be removed and trees replanted, or where a new group or growth of trees that have to be planted, be it installation of tree samplings or planting of instant trees, NParks and HDB, where HDB manages the green areas, could initiate a consultation process with residents.

sections.label: Residents voting tree options
sections.summary: NParks could direct residents to a webpage presenting tree options to vote on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For example, where such decisions need to be made, NParks could direct residents to a webpage that presents different tree options that they could vote on.

sections.label: Invasive species entering reserves
sections.summary: The amendment regulates animal release but does not address invasive species entering reserves by random chance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Many of these are large-scale developments like condominiums and strata landed housing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This amendment regulating the release or abandonment of animals into reserves through waterways is a good one, but it does not address one major issue, which is the potential of invasive species entering the reserves, not by design or choice, but by random chance, such as nonindigenous declarative plants favoured by condominium developers reproducing in the reserves, or exotic pets owned by residents, escaping accidentally into the reserves without the conscious choice of the residents to release them.

sections.label: Botanic Gardens land reduction
sections.summary: Clause 23 reduces Botanic Gardens land by 151 sqm, and the reason for this reduction was asked.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Clause 23 will result in a reduction of 151 sqm of land from the Botanic Gardens.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It is a small reduction but I would just like to clarify what is the reason for this reduction.

sections.label: NParks staffing for policing
sections.summary: It was asked to what extent NParks envisages inducting more staff to police nature reserves in parks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Separately, but related to the main point, to what extent does NParks envisage that it will induct more staff in this way to police nature reserves in parks?

sections.label: Animal release outside nature reserves
sections.summary: Clause 5 extends the offence of releasing or abandoning animals to rivers, streams, canals and watercourses outside nature reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: In this new amendment, there is one area of focus under clause 5 which deals with the release or abandonment of animals into any river, stream, canal or watercourse, not just within, but now also outside of nature reserves.

sections.label: NParks entry to check trees
sections.summary: Clauses 14 and 18 of the Parks and Trees Act empower NParks officers or contractors to enter to ascertain tree or plant conditions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Under clauses 14 and 18 of the Parks and Trees Act, NParks officers or their contractors are now empowered to enter to ascertain tree or plant conditions.

sections.label: Support for new marine park
sections.summary: The speaker gives utmost support to the designation of the new marine park.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: On the designation of the new marine park, I give my utmost support.

sections.label: Mitigating impact on nature spot
sections.summary: The speaker asks how NParks intends to address concerns and mitigate negative impact on a fragile nature spot.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: How then does NParks intend to address these concerns and mitigate any negative impact on this fragile nature spot?

sections.label: Developing the landscape industry
sections.summary: The speaker asks what areas NParks will take on to develop the landscape industry, citing short tenancies and industry fears.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Feedback from the landscape industry has been that they feel very hard-pressed to develop further because of the short tenancies that they face.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: And previous arrangements have been such that they are very fearful as they come close to the renewal of their leases, whether they can continue or they will have to close their businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: It is very land intensive and very capital intensive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: What are the areas that NParks will be taking on to further develop the landscape industry in Singapore, so that we can continue to have a city in a garden?

sections.label: Marine park protection and oil spill
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes clause 2 designating marine park as public park, citing a 300-tonne oil spill in the Straits of Johor.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: These animals and the marine biodiversity of the Straits of Singapore are part of our natural heritage and should be protected and preserved.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am thus glad that amendments made to the Bill in clause 2 will designate "marine park" as a type of "public park" and that NParks will have juridical control and enforcement rights over A good example that illustrates this point is the recent 300-tonne oil spill that occurred in the Straits of Johor when two ships collided northeast of Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Those responsible for the oil spill must be held accountable for the disaster and the amendments to the Bill will hopefully give NParks more authority to take the appropriate action.

sections.label: Non-NParks land amendment
sections.summary: The proposed amendment would include non-NParks managed land under the Act, allowing prosecution of those who damage trees and plants there.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Another proposed amendment to the Act I would like to speak on is the proposal to include non-NParks managed land under the Act as indicated in clauses 2 and 4.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This is, in my opinion, a positive amendment as this would allow those who damage trees and plants in these areas to be prosecuted.

sections.label: NParks officers entry authority
sections.summary: Clauses 14 and 18 would give NParks officers authority to enter premises to issue maintenance notices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The proposed changes to the Act in clauses 14 and 18 would give NParks officers the authority to enter various premises to issue maintenance notices.

sections.label: Interpreting danger under clause
sections.summary: The speaker asks how NParks would interpret danger under the amended clause, calling the premise subjective and seeking greater clarity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Like my colleague, Er Dr Lee Bee Wah, I am also interested to know how NParks would interpret what constitutes "danger" under the amended clause.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I believe that most of us would understand "danger" in the most obvious sense, such as when a branch or tree could potentially fall on someone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For example, would the presence of a bee-hive or toxic and poisonous sap from trees be regarded as "dangerous?" Would trees that regularly shed leaves that might be a hazard on a slippery floor during rainy days be considered "dangerous?" The premise of what constitutes "danger" is, therefore, subjective and I believe greater clarity in the interpretation of what is "dangerous" is necessary in order for the law to have its full desired effect.

sections.label: Sitting suspended and NParks authority
sections.summary: The sitting was suspended from 4.00 pm until 4.20 pm, and the speaker notes amendments would give NParks more authority.

sentences.speaker: Mdm Speaker
sentences.text: Sitting accordingly suspended  at 4.00 pm until 4.20 pm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I am pleased to note that amendments to the Bill will give NParks more authority to perform its duties.

sections.label: Monitoring contractors and arborists
sections.summary: The speaker suggests NParks could monitor contractors and their appointed arborist and be given authority to act when necessary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Perhaps NParks can step in to monitor the work of contractors and their appointed arborist and be accorded the authority to take action when necessary.

sections.label: Neighbourly disputes referred to mediation
sections.summary: The amendment dictates that neighbourly disputes will be referred for mediation and community resolution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The amendment has dictated that neighbourly disputes will be referred for mediation and community resolution.

sections.label: Grass-cutting noise health effects
sections.summary: Long-term exposure to noise from nearby grass-cutting and tree-cutting can cause health problems, and NParks should help residents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Considering that many of the houses are in very close proximity, long-term exposure to the noise can lead to a myriad of health problems, from tinnitus and stress to hearing loss.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I hope NParks will look into this and help residents to safeguard against inconsiderate grass-cutting and tree-cutting practices with levels of noise.

sections.label: Marine parks in Parks and Trees Act
sections.summary: The Bill includes marine parks in the Parks and Trees Act, giving NParks jurisdiction over the seas for the first time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As such, I applaud the Bill for the inclusion of "marine parks" in the Parks and Trees Act (PTA), giving NParks − for the first time − jurisdiction over the seas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This will provide the Sisters' Island Marine Park with greater protection against destructive behaviour.

sections.label: Acts not allowed in marine park
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister to clarify specifically what acts are not allowed in the marine park.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister clarify specifically what acts are not allowed in the marine park?

sections.label: Extending NParks jurisdiction to coastal areas
sections.summary: The speaker asks if NParks jurisdiction could extend to coastal Nature Reserves and coastal parks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Next, in order for NParks to fully protect our marine biodiversity from destructive behaviours, could the Ministry look into making similar amendments to extend full jurisdiction by NParks to coastal Nature Reserves like the Sungei Buloh Wetland Reserve and Labrador Nature Reserve, as well as coastal parks, such as the Changi Beach Park, Pasir Ris Park, East Coast Park and Chek Jawa?

sections.label: Prohibiting release of exotic species
sections.summary: The speaker proposes prohibiting release of exotic species anywhere in Singapore, citing enforcement difficulties and red-eared sliders harming local turtles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: How will NParks be able to prove what he or she knows or does not know?

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I foresee some technical difficulties with enforcement and thus propose an alternative solution, which is to prohibit the release of exotic species anywhere, on land or in water, in Singapore, and not simply to restrict this to certain areas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Animals are not stationary and have the freedom to travel from unrestricted areas to nature reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Hence, I see little rationale in creating demarcations when prohibiting the release of animals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For example, the red-eared sliders, which are native to North America, have caused numbers of our local Asian box turtles to drop significantly.

sections.label: Nature in children's curriculum
sections.summary: The speaker proposes systematically incorporating nature into children's curriculum.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As such, I would like to propose that we systematically incorporate nature into our children's curriculum.

sections.label: School visits to parks
sections.summary: Suggests encouraging Primary and Secondary schools to make quarterly visits to parks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Perhaps a good way to start is to encourage our Primary and Secondary schools to have quarterly visits to our parks.

sections.label: NParks operating grant funding
sections.summary: States NParks receives a modest operating grant of slightly over $200 million annually, about 0.3% of the overall Budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Yet, against rising expectations of our residents and sharply increased manpower cost for maintenance and pruning, NParks receives a relatively modest operating grant of slightly over $200 million annually.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: To put that in perspective, that is around 0.3% of our overall Budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In fact, NParks' strong corporate partnerships and its ability to attract top business leaders to its board are testimony of NParks' entrepreneurial spirit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: But at some point, we might approach a situation where the budget might not match NParks' enlarged mission.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: With the economy where it is, resources across the Government are understandably tight.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: However, I do hope that when the opportunity arises, NParks will be allocated more funding to deliver on its mission and to strengthen outreach.

sections.label: Wildlife encounters and experiences
sections.summary: Recounts seeing a baby Big Eye Green Whip snake and Sambar deers descended from a Mandai zoo break-out.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We also chanced upon a baby Big Eye Green Whip snake.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: We even also learnt that the Sambar deers that we occasionally see there came from the descendants of a major Mandai zoo break-out in the late 1970s.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: It was a beautiful experience and it stayed in our memories.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I hope that all Singaporeans, especially our children, can enjoy similar experiences, and develop a deep love for our land.

sections.label: Tree protection and marine park
sections.summary: Describes existing legislative levers protecting trees and amending the Act for Sisters' Islands Marine Park areas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked whether NParks could monitor construction damage to ensure that trees are not damaged in the course of works.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: There are existing legislative levers in the Act to ensure that trees are not indiscriminately damaged.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: For trees that are specifically protected, like those in heritage road green buffers and road verges, as well as mature trees in tree conservation areas and vacant lands, NParks works closely with site arborists, contractors and developers to ensure that no damage is caused.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Mr Darryl David, Mr Louis Ng, Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef and Assoc Prof Daniel Goh spoke about the Sisters' Islands Marine Park.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: To clarify, we are amending the Act to make clear that the marine and foreshore areas of the Sisters' Islands Marine Park are a type of "public park".

sections.label: New marine park rules
sections.summary: States NParks will make new rules specific to marine parks in due course.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: NParks will make new rules that are specific to marine parks in due course.

sections.label: Marine park walks and plans
sections.summary: Notes guided intertidal walks and dive trips, and plans for a boardwalk, intertidal pools and floating pontoon.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: It has also worked with marine nature groups on guided intertidal walks and dive trips at the Marine Park.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We have further plans to develop a boardwalk, intertidal pools and a floating pontoon at Big Sister's Island.

sections.label: Released aquarium fish harm native species
sections.summary: Released Asian Arowana in Nee Soon Swamp Forest harm native species, so NParks continues Operation No Release awareness campaign.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: For example, some Asian Arowana, which is an aquarium fish that is not native to Singapore, have been released by members of the public in very sensitive freshwater habitats like Nee Soon Swamp Forest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The Arowanas then gorge themselves on our highly threatened native fish and crustacean species, and caused ecological damage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: They are often unable to cope with the new environment and That is why NParks will continue to work with relevant agencies and community groups on "Operation No Release", which spreads awareness on the harm caused by this behaviour.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: This year's campaign is expected to take place in May.

sections.label: Singapore Botanic Gardens size growth
sections.summary: SBG grew from 53 hectares in 2015 to 82 hectares today with Bukit Timah, Tyersall and Gallop additions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In fact, SBG was 53 hectares in 2015 and, today, it is 82 hectares, with the inclusion of 11 hectares at the Bukit Timah core, 10 hectares from the Tyersall Learning Forest and eight hectares from Gallop extension.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: So, SBG has, indeed, grown even as we took a bit of the frontage for the MRT exit or entrance.

sections.label: Invasive species near nature reserves
sections.summary: Concern about invasive plants and non-native pets entering nature reserves led to a Bill clause prohibiting animal releases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Mr Leon Perera also spoke about developments along the fringes of nature reserves, such as Bukit Timah and Central Catchment Nature Reserves, and is concerned about whether invasive plant species as well as pets that are not native to Singapore might then enter our nature reserves and cause ecological damage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We are always concerned about invasive species and that, really, is the genesis of that clause in the Bill that allows us to prohibit the release of animals into water bodies that lead to nature reserves.

sections.label: Geh Min on nature reserves species
sections.summary: In 2004 Dr Geh Min sought a marine park and said some nature reserves have more species than North America.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In 2004, Dr Geh Min, the former President of the Nature Society, at the Second Reading of the Parks and Trees (Amendment) Bill, apart from articulating a desire for a marine park − so, 10 years on after that, we have established it − she also said that, in fact, some of our nature reserves have more species in plants and animals than, say, the whole of the North American continent.

sections.label: NParks educational programmes annually
sections.summary: NParks organises around 2,400 educational programmes yearly, including guided tours to the Botanic Gardens and nature reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: NParks organises around 2,400 educational programmes annually, including guided tours to the Botanic Gardens and nature reserves.

sections.label: Nursery land leases monthly rentals
sections.summary: Based on feedback, NParks will tender nursery lands on three, plus three, plus three leases, allowing monthly rentals instead of upfront premiums.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Based on their feedback, NParks will be tendering out nursery lands on three, plus three, plus three leases since this model allows some nurseries to pay monthly rentals rather than upfront land premiums.

sections.label: Nursery land in Nee Soon South
sections.summary: Feedback on nurseries in Bah Soon Pah, Nee Soon South, is considered and will be announced later, with overall nursery land possibly less than currently available.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
sentences.text: I know this as I have a nursery in Bah Soon Pah which is in Nee Soon South.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We have taken all this feedback into consideration and will announce at an appropriate juncture.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The overall land available for nurseries may not be as much as is available currently.

sections.label: Marine Park stakeholder needs and protection
sections.summary: Managing needs of stakeholders like recreation users, boatmen, divers and biodiversity supporters, and amending the Act to confer protection on the Marine Park.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: It involves managing the needs, wants and concerns of different stakeholders − people who go there for recreation, people who are boatmen, people who like to dive, people who are passionate about biodiversity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: We have amended this Act in order to allow us to confer the protection on the Marine Park that we feel it needs from the last three years of experience.
